question: What labelling requirements apply to Ayurveda Aahara products?
answer:
**India**



- Labelling of Ayurveda Aahara must comply with the Food Safety and Standards (Labelling and Display) Regulations, 2020 and the specific labelling provisions of the Ayurveda Aahara Regulations. [1]

- Every label must state the intended purpose of the product, the target consumer group and the recommended duration of use. [1]

- The front of the pack must display the words “AYURVEDA AAHARA” in close proximity to the product name or brand and the logo prescribed in Schedule E of the regulations. [2]

- An advisory warning “ONLY FOR DIETARY USE” must be prominently printed on the label. [2]

- The label must contain a statement that the Ayurveda Aahara is not a substitute for a varied diet. [2]

- Any warnings, precautions, known side‑effects, contraindications and published product or drug interactions must be disclosed on the label. [2]

- The label must advise that the product should be stored out of reach of children and that it is for oral consumption only, not for parenteral use. [2]

- The label must not claim that the product prevents, treats or cures any human disease; any health or disease‑risk‑reduction claims must follow the Food Safety and Standards (Advertising and Claims) Regulations, 2018 and be approved as per Schedule B of the Ayurveda Aahara Regulations. [1]



**Sources**



[1] [Food Safety and Standards (Ayurveda Aahara) Regulations 2022: original Gazette](https://stg-old.fssai.gov.in/upload/notifications/2022/05/62789a20b54bdGazette_Notification_Ayurveda_Aahara_09_05_2022.pdf#page=16) | PDF page: 16 | https://stg-old.fssai.gov.in/upload/notifications/2022/05/62789a20b54bdGazette_Notification_Ayurveda_Aahara_09_05_2022.pdf | Retrieved: 2026-09-28

[2] [Food Safety and Standards (Ayurveda Aahara) Regulations 2022: original Gazette](https://stg-old.fssai.gov.in/upload/notifications/2022/05/62789a20b54bdGazette_Notification_Ayurveda_Aahara_09_05_2022.pdf#page=17) | PDF page: 17 | https://stg-old.fssai.gov.in/upload/notifications/2022/05/62789a20b54bdGazette_Notification_Ayurveda_Aahara_09_05_2022.pdf | Retrieved: 2026-09-28

question: Can I patent a traditional Ayurvedic formulation?
answer:
**India**



- A formulation that is part of traditional Ayurvedic knowledge is excluded from patentability under Section 3(p) of the Indian Patents Act, 1970, which states that an invention that is traditional knowledge or an aggregation of known properties of traditionally known components is not an invention. [1]

- If the formulation is merely a mixture of known Ayurvedic ingredients whose combined effect is only the aggregation of the individual properties, it is also excluded under Section 3(e) as a “substance obtained by a mere admixture resulting only in the aggregation of the properties of the components thereof”. [1]

- Guidelines for processing patent applications state that traditional knowledge is in the public domain and therefore does not qualify as an invention under Section 2(1)(j); consequently, any patent claim based on such knowledge is not allowable. [4]

- The same guidelines note that extracts or uses of plants already disclosed in Ayurvedic texts are not novel and lack inventive step, so a claim directed to such a formulation would be rejected for lack of novelty and inventive step. [6]



**Sources**



[1] [Patents Act 1970: Section 3 Inventions Not Patentable (Complete clauses a to p)](https://ipindia.gov.in/acts-patents.htm) | https://ipindia.gov.in/acts-patents.htm

[4] [Guidelines for Processing Patent Applications Relating to Traditional Knowledge and Biological Material (2012)](https://ipindia.gov.in/frontend/pdf/patents/guidelines/Guidelines%20for%20Processing%20of%20Patent%20Applications%20relating%20to%20Traditional%20Knowledge%20and%20Biological%20Material%20-%202012.pdf#page=2) | PDF page: 2 | https://ipindia.gov.in/frontend/pdf/patents/guidelines/Guidelines%20for%20Processing%20of%20Patent%20Applications%20relating%20to%20Traditional%20Knowledge%20and%20Biological%20Material%20-%202012.pdf | Retrieved: 2026-09-28

[6] [Guidelines for Processing Patent Applications Relating to Traditional Knowledge and Biological Material (2012)](https://ipindia.gov.in/frontend/pdf/patents/guidelines/Guidelines%20for%20Processing%20of%20Patent%20Applications%20relating%20to%20Traditional%20Knowledge%20and%20Biological%20Material%20-%202012.pdf#page=5) | PDF page: 5 | https://ipindia.gov.in/frontend/pdf/patents/guidelines/Guidelines%20for%20Processing%20of%20Patent%20Applications%20relating%20to%20Traditional%20Knowledge%20and%20Biological%20Material%20-%202012.pdf | Retrieved: 2026-09-28

question: How does the Budapest Treaty help with microorganism deposits for patents?
answer:
**International (destination-specific rules require a named market)**



- Contracting States must recognize, for patent procedures, the deposit of a microorganism with any international depositary authority, including the fact and date of the deposit and that a sample furnished is a sample of the deposited microorganism. [1]

- The Budapest System allows a single deposit of a microorganism to be recognised throughout the countries that are parties to the system, providing a practical mechanism for obtaining patent protection for biotechnological inventions in many jurisdictions. [3]

- International depositary authorities must store the deposited biological material in a viable and uncontaminated condition and must provide samples to interested parties in accordance with the Treaty and national law, supporting the disclosure requirement of patent law. [4]

- No Contracting State may require compliance with requirements different from or additional to those provided in the Budapest Treaty and its Regulations. [6]
